input: This executive summary presents an appraisal of a proposed heat-recovery retrofit at the food plant, where refrigeration currently accounts for a substantial 1935 MWh of electricity consumption per year. According to projections provided by the equipment vendor, the retrofit is expected to save 17% of that use, which corresponds to a derived saving of 329 MWh per year at the vendor figure. The capital cost of the project is $498k, and at an electricity price of $0.11 per kWh, the derived annual saving works out at $36k, giving a derived simple payback of 13.8 years. It is important to note that this represents a considerable capital commitment of $498k set against an annual saving of just $36k, and a payback of 13.8 years is, by any measure, a long horizon over which to recover the investment. Crucially, the saving figure is a vendor projection that has not been measured at this plant, and refrigeration load in the summer peak month has not been modelled, meaning that the appraisal rests on assumptions that remain unverified in the conditions that matter most. In light of these considerations, it is recommended that a metered trial be carried out on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision is taken, with the plant engineer owning the trial and reporting the measured results, so that the eventual decision can be based on evidence gathered at this plant rather than on projections alone, however favourable those projections may appear at first sight.
target: A metered trial on one of the three refrigeration lines should come before any capital decision on the heat-recovery retrofit; the plant engineer owns the trial. The plant uses 1935 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration. The equipment vendor projects a saving of 17% of that use, a derived saving of 329 MWh per year at the vendor figure. Capital cost is $498k. At an electricity price of $0.11 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $36k, and the derived simple payback is 13.8 years. The trade-off is $498k of capital now against $36k of saving per year at the vendor's figure. The saving is a vendor projection and was not measured at this plant. Refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, and the peak month is where the retrofit case is strongest or weakest, because recovered heat follows the load that produces it. A payback of 13.8 years is long against the working life of the equipment the retrofit would be fitted to, and it lengthens further if the realised saving falls below the projection. The trial settles the point the appraisal cannot. Metering one line through a full load cycle gives a measured saving at this plant, on this refrigeration load, with the projection tested against the plant's own meters. The trial also prices the disruption honestly: one line carries the instrumentation and the operating changes, and the other lines run untouched as the comparison. The plant engineer's report should state the measured saving per unit of refrigeration load, so that the figure for the full retrofit can be rebuilt from it line by line. The capital decision waits for the trial result, and the result it waits for is a measured saving, not a revised projection.
